This review systematically addresses their classification, botanical sources, isolation techniques, and biogenesis pathways. Comprehensive compositional analyses reveal a diverse cargo of proteins, lipids, nucleic acids, and metabolites that support their biological activity. Plant-derived extracellular vesicles possess intrinsic anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, antineoplastic, and regenerative properties, while also serving as efficient natural drug-delivery systems. We then summarize their therapeutic applications in nervous system tumors, traumatic neurological injuries, neurodegenerative diseases, and neuropsychiatric disorders. Although substantial challenges remain in standardizing isolation protocols and optimizing targeted delivery, plant-derived extracellular vesicles offer a sustainable, highly biocompatible, and scalable alternative to mammalian-derived extracellular vesicles. Future research should focus on harnessing their unique characteristics to improve cargo engineering and facilitate transport across physiological barriers, including the blood-brain barrier. Addressing these challenges and further optimizing the functionality of plant-derived extracellular vesicles could profoundly reshape the landscape of neurological therapeutics.

title: Altered intersubject variability of functional connectivity in gray and white matter underlying neurocognition and genetic profiles in neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.
abstract: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder is an autoimmune disease that causes inflammatory damage to the central nervous system. While alterations in functional connectivity have been reported in neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, changes in intersubject variability of functional connectivity within gray matter and white matter are not yet understood. A total of 66 patients with neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder and 71 healthy controls were recruited. We compared intersubject variability of functional connectivity between patients with neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder and healthy controls and performed subgroup analyses comparing neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder patients with and without a history of optic neuritis. We also examined the associations between intersubject variability of functional connectivity alterations and disease duration, clinical disability, and cognitive scores. We combined our imaging results with those of the Allen Human Brain Atlas to conduct transcriptome-neuroimaging association analyses, identified gene expression profiles linked to intersubject variability of functional connectivity alterations and characterized their potential biological functions. Compared with healthy controls, patients with neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder showed widespread increases in intersubject variability of functional connectivity. Notable gray matter alterations included the precentral and postcentral gyri; extensive occipital areas; and the insula, putamen, and thalamus. The corresponding white matter changes involved the fornix, corticospinal tract, widespread corona radiata, cingulum, and uncinate fasciculus. Compared with patients without optic neuritis, the optic neuritis subgroup exhibited distinct intersubject variability of functional connectivity alterations in specific regions, such as the inferior parietal lobule, angular gyrus, thalamus, fornix, and internal capsule. Clinically, only white matter-intersubject variability of functional connectivity correlated significantly with physical disability and cognitive processing speed and was not significantly associated with disease duration. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that genes positively associated with white matter-intersubject variability of functional connectivity were enriched in synaptic plasticity and cognition, while negatively associated genes were enriched in oxidative stress. Additionally, genes positively associated with the gray matter-intersubject variability of functional connectivity were enriched in myelination and lipid biosynthesis, whereas genes negatively associated with the gray matter-intersubject variability of functional connectivity were involved in synapse organization. In conclusion, our study revealed alterations in gray matter- and white matter-intersubject variability of functional connectivity across neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder and clinical subtypes. We demonstrate that changes in white matter-intersubject variability of functional connectivity correlate with clinical disability and neurocognition. Linking these connectivity patterns with gene expression profiles may provide insights into the underlying pathophysiology of neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.

title: Development of a biomimetic manganese dioxide nanoreactor delivery system: Combination of biomimetic platelet/M2 microglia hybrid membrane with Astragaloside IV for the treatment of ischemic stroke.
abstract: Conventional nanotherapeutics suffer from rapid immune clearance and insufficient accumulation in ischemic lesions. To overcome these bottlenecks, a stimuli-responsive biomimetic immunomodulatory delivery system was engineered by fusing platelet and M2 microglial membranes onto hollow mesoporous manganese dioxide nanoparticles loaded with the neuroprotective drug Astragaloside IV. The results show that this integrated nanoplatform fully leverages the synergistic properties of its biomimetic shell. Tracing the nanoparticles with the fluorescent dye Did revealed that the integrated nanoplatform exhibited more pronounced fluorescent enrichment in ischemic brain tissue; both in vivo and ex vivo imaging supported its specific homing ability. In a mouse model of middle cerebral artery occlusion and reperfusion, the platform significantly reduced the extent of cerebral infarction, alleviated neuronal damage caused by ischemia-reperfusion, and improved neurovascular integrity and neurological function. Furthermore, the platform mitigated oxidative stress in ischemic brain tissue, curtailed the inflammatory response, and facilitated a transition in microglial phenotype toward an anti-inflammatory and reparative state. Bioinformatics results indicate that this platform significantly alters gene expression profiles following cerebral ischemia-reperfusion. Differential expression and functional enrichment analyses further point to biological processes related to inflammation and immune regulation. These findings demonstrate that this biomimetic targeted nanoplatform integrates biomimetic targeting, reactive oxygen species scavenging, and immune modulation capabilities, thereby providing a new therapeutic platform technology for the precise delivery of therapeutic agents and the remodeling of the pathological microenvironment in ischemic stroke.

title: Absence of familial adult myoclonic epilepsy-associated intronic repeat expansions in SAMD12, STARD7, and MARCHF6 genes in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy with tremor.
abstract: We investigated whether intronic repeat expansions in the SAMD12, STARD7, and MARCHF6 genes are present in individuals with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy (JME) and tremor. Given that tremor is a shared feature with familial adult myoclonic epilepsy (FAME), we hypothesized that this phenotype may reflect a common genetic basis involving FAME-associated pentanucleotide repeat expansions. The study included 31 individuals with JME and tremor (17/31 [54.8%] females, mean age at genetic testing = 34.4 ± 13.8 years) and 100 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Genomic DNA was analyzed using repeat-primed polymerase chain reaction and fragment analysis to detect intronic TTTCA repeat expansions in the three established FAME-associated genes. No pathogenic repeat expansions were identified in SAMD12, STARD7, or MARCHF6 among individuals with JME and tremor. The frequency of intronic pentanucleotide repeat expansions did not differ between cases and controls. This is a comprehensive analysis assessing three FAME-associated repeat-expansion loci in a clinically well-characterized cohort of individuals with JME and tremor. Our findings do not support a major contribution of these FAME-associated loci to tremor in this cohort, suggesting that those intronic repeats did not contribute to genetic susceptibility to the tremor in JME. Further studies are required to identify the factors associated with this phenotype.

title: siRNA-Mediated RNF213 Depletion Aggravates Inflammatory Hypoxia-Induced Endothelial Dysfunction and Alters Endothelial-Smooth-Muscle Communication in an In Vitro Model Relevant to Moyamoya Disease.
abstract: Moyamoya disease is a progressive cerebrovascular disorder associated with variants in ring finger protein 213 (RNF213), endothelial dysfunction and pathological arterial remodelling. However, the relationship between reduced RNF213 abundance, inflammatory hypoxia and endothelial-smooth-muscle communication remains incompletely understood. This study investigated the effects of small interfering RNA (siRNA)-mediated RNF213 depletion in primary human brain microvascular endothelial cells exposed to combined hypoxia, tumour necrosis factor alpha (TNF-α) and interferon gamma (IFN-γ). Endothelial viability, proliferation, apoptosis, migration, angiogenic network formation and barrier integrity were evaluated. Conditioned-medium and indirect co-culture systems were subsequently used to examine responses in primary human brain vascular smooth muscle cells. Combined RNF213 depletion and inflammatory hypoxia reduced endothelial viability and proliferation, increased apoptosis, impaired migration and network formation, and compromised barrier integrity. Barrier impairment was demonstrated by decreased transendothelial electrical resistance, increased dextran permeability and disruption of vascular endothelial cadherin (VE-cadherin), zonula occludens-1 (ZO-1), claudin-5 and occludin. RNF213 depletion also enhanced endothelial inflammatory activation. Conditioned medium from RNF213-depleted inflammatory-hypoxic endothelial cells was associated with increased smooth-muscle-cell proliferation, migration and colony formation. These responses were accompanied by reduced contractile-marker expression and increased secreted phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1), Krüppel-like factor 4 (KLF4), fibronectin 1 (FN1) and matrix metalloproteinase 9 (MMP9), consistent with transition toward a synthetic, matrix-remodelling phenotype. The responsible endothelial-derived mediator or combination of mediators was not identified. Selected findings were reproduced using indirect co-culture and an independent siRNA targeting a different RNF213 sequence. These findings support an association between siRNA-mediated RNF213 depletion, endothelial stress susceptibility and altered endothelial-smooth-muscle communication in an in-vitro model relevant to Moyamoya disease. RNF213 re-expression or orthogonal genetic validation will be required to establish RNF213-specific causality.Clinical Trial Number None.

title: Gut Microbiota in Alzheimer's Disease and Healthy Aging: Mechanisms, Prevention Strategies and Healthcare Burden.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by cognitive decline associated with oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, tau neurofibrillary tangles, amyloid-beta plaque deposition, and metabolic dysfunction. Increasing evidence suggests that the gut microbiota plays an important role in AD pathogenesis through the microbiota-gut-brain axis. This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the role of the gut microbiota in AD and healthy aging, with a particular focus on microbiota-targeted preventive and therapeutic strategies and their potential to influence disease progression. Recent studies have demonstrated that alterations in gut microbial composition are closely associated with AD. Patients with AD commonly exhibit a reduced abundance of short-chain fatty acid-producing bacteria and an increased prevalence of lipopolysaccharide-producing taxa, supporting a mechanistic link between microbial dysbiosis, systemic inflammation, and neurodegeneration. Emerging evidence indicates that dietary patterns, prebiotics, probiotics, synbiotics, postbiotics, and microbiota-based therapies, including fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), may beneficially modulate gut microbial composition and influence AD-related pathophysiological processes. In addition, lifestyle factors such as sleep quality and physical activity have been increasingly recognized for their interactions with the gut-brain axis and their potential to affect cognitive health. Current evidence highlights the gut microbiota as a promising therapeutic target in AD prevention and management. Microbiota-directed interventions, together with healthy dietary and lifestyle modifications, may help attenuate neuroinflammation, improve metabolic homeostasis, and delay cognitive decline. Furthermore, given the substantial global economic burden of AD, microbiota-focused preventive strategies may contribute not only to improving clinical outcomes but also to reducing long-term healthcare and societal costs. Future longitudinal and interventional studies are needed to establish causal relationships and determine the efficacy of microbiota-based therapies in AD.

title: Management of shift work disorder: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline.
journal: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine
abstract: This guideline establishes recommendations for the treatment of SWD. The American Academy of Sleep Medicine (AASM) commissioned a task force of experts in sleep and circadian medicine to develop recommendations and assign strengths based on a systematic review of the literature and an assessment of the evidence using the GRADE process. The task force summarized the relevant literature and the quality of evidence, the balance of benefits and harms, patient values and preferences, and resource use considerations supporting the recommendations. The AASM Board of Directors approved the final recommendations. The following recommendations are intended as a guide for clinicians in choosing specific treatment(s) for symptoms of excessive sleepiness and/or insomnia, and for circadian adaptation in adults with SWD. Each recommendation statement is assigned a strength (e.g., "Strong" or "Conditional"). For SWD, there were only "conditional" recommendations for or against (i.e., "We suggest…") and those requiring the clinician to use clinical knowledge and experience and consider the individual patient's values and preferences to determine the best course of action. Interventions in recommendation statements were compared to no treatment. Adults with SWD with symptoms of excessive sleepiness associated with work schedule: 1. In adults with SWD with excessive sleepiness, the AASM suggests the use of armodafinil or modafinil taken 30 to 60 minutes prior to the night shift over no armodafinil or modafinil (Conditional recommendation, moderate certainty of evidence). 2. In adults with SWD with excessive sleepiness, the AASM suggests the use of bright light over no bright light during the night shift (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence). Individuals with SWD who exhibit insomnia and daytime function impairments may also benefit from using bright light during their night shift. 3. In adults with SWD with excessive sleepiness, the AASM suggests the use of caffeine taken prior to and/or during the night shift over no caffeine (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence). Caffeine intake close to bedtime can disrupt sleep onset and quality, which may exacerbate symptoms of SWD. 4. In adults with SWD with excessive sleepiness, the AASM suggests the use of a clockwise rotating shift schedule over a counterclockwise rotating shift schedule (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence). 5. In adults with SWD with excessive sleepiness, the AASM suggests taking a nap over no nap prior to the night shift (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence). Sleep inertia occurring soon after the nap may temporarily increase sleepiness, decrease cognitive performance, and increase accident risk. Allowing adequate time for resolution of sleep inertia prior to driving or performing other safety-sensitive behaviors may be needed to reduce these risks. 6. In adults with SWD with excessive sleepiness, the AASM suggests either not eating or eating a snack rather than eating a full meal during the night shift (Conditional recommendation, low certainty of evidence). 7. In adults with SWD with excessive sleepiness, the AASM suggests the combination of caffeine and bright light over the combination of no caffeine and no bright light (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence). Caffeine intake close to bedtime can disrupt sleep onset and quality, which may exacerbate symptoms of SWD. 8. In adults with SWD with excessive sleepiness, the AASM suggests the combination of taking a nap and caffeine over the combination of no nap and no caffeine prior to the night shift (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence). Adults with SWD with sleep disturbance/insomnia: 9. In adults with SWD with daytime sleep disturbance/insomnia the AASM suggests the use of CBT-I over no CBT-I (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence). 10. In adults with SWD with daytime sleep disturbance/insomnia following the night shift, the AASM suggests the use of melatonin over no melatonin (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence). 11. In adults with SWD with sleep disturbance/insomnia, when transitioning from daytime to nighttime sleep, the AASM suggests the use of melatonin over no melatonin for night sleep following shift work (Conditional recommendation, low certainty of evidence). 12. In adults with SWD who desire to take a nap prior to the first night shift, the AASM suggests the use of melatonin over no melatonin prior to the nap (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence). Melatonin may temporarily increase sleepiness, decrease cognitive performance, and increase accident risk. Allowing adequate time for resolution of sleepiness prior to driving, returning to work or performing other safety-sensitive behaviors may be needed to reduce these risks. 13. In adults with SWD with daytime sleep disturbance/insomnia, the AASM suggests the use of ramelteon or other melatonin receptor agonists over no melatonin receptor agonist (Conditional recommendation, low certainty of evidence). 14. In adults with SWD with daytime sleep disturbance/insomnia, the AASM suggests the use of suvorexant or other dual orexin receptor antagonists over no dual orexin receptor antagonists (Conditional recommendation, low certainty of evidence). 15. In adults with SWD with daytime sleep disturbance/insomnia, the AASM suggests against the use of triazolam and other benzodiazepines (conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence). Adults with SWD seeking circadian adaptation: 16. In adults with SWD seeking circadian adaptation to the night shift, the AASM suggests the use of bright light over no bright light during the night shift (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty). For individuals who work rotating or frequently changing shifts, circadian adaptation is not a realistic goal of treatment and therefore they would not be expected to benefit from this intervention. The evidence supporting this recommendation came from studies in which individuals reached partial circadian adaptation to the night shift. 17. In adults with SWD seeking circadian adaptation to the night shift, the AASM suggests the combination of bright light at night and fixed daytime sleep timing over the combination of no bright light and no fixed sleep timing (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence). For individuals who work rotating or frequently changing shifts, circadian adaptation is not a realistic goal of treatment and therefore they would not be expected to benefit from this intervention. The evidence supporting this recommendation came from studies in which individuals reached partial circadian adaptation to the night shift. 18. In adults with SWD seeking circadian adaptation to the night shift, the AASM suggests the combination of bright light at night, fixed daytime sleep timing, and reduced-light-transmittance glasses in the morning over the combination of no bright light, no fixed sleep timing, and no reduced-light-transmittance glasses (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence). Remark 1 : For individuals who work rotating or frequently changing shifts, circadian adaptation is not a realistic goal of treatment and therefore they would not be expected to benefit from this intervention. The evidence supporting this recommendation came from studies in which individuals reached partial circadian adaptation to the night shift. Remark 2: Attention to driving safety is important when wearing reduced-light-transmittance glasses. Other considerations for adults with SWD: 19. In adults with SWD who are working either an 8-hour or 12-hour night shift, the AASM does not suggest working one shift duration over the other (Conditional recommendation, very low certainty of evidence). This recommendation does not consider other shift durations, rotation, or the number of consecutive shifts. This guideline did not look at shift durations exceeding 12 hours. The total number of hours worked per week ranged from 36 to 52.

title: Hemodynamic responses to clinical dosages of dopamine and dobutamine in dogs with hypotension under isoflurane anesthesia.
abstract: While dopamine and dobutamine are widely used in anesthetized dogs, clinical evidence supporting their use remains limited. We aimed to compare the hemodynamic responses to clinical dosages of dopamine and dobutamine in dogs with hypotension undergoing elective orthopedic surgery under fentanyl-isoflurane anesthesia. The pressor effects at clinical dosages (2-8 µg/kg/min) of dopamine (n = 15) and dobutamine (n = 15) for hypotension were compared and confirmed using the ramped-rate infusion protocol in 30 dogs. The following hemodynamic parameters measured by invasive arterial blood pressure and transesophageal echocardiographic monitoring were analyzed: heart rate (HR), systolic (SAP), mean (MAP), diastolic arterial pressure (DAP), stroke volume index (SVI), cardiac index (CI), and systemic vascular resistance index (SVRI). The proportion of dogs that achieved the treatment goal (MAP: 70-89 mmHg) was 93% (dopamine responders, 14/15 dogs) in the dopamine group and 53% (dobutamine responders, 8/15 dogs) in the dobutamine group, with a significantly higher probability in the dopamine group (P = 0.035, a risk difference of 40% [95% confidence interval: 8.2-63.9%]). In dopamine responders, significant increases were observed in SAP, MAP, DAP, SVI and CI, whereas no significant changes were observed in HR and SVRI. In conclusion, the pressor effect was more likely to be observed at the clinical dosage of dopamine than that of dobutamine for treating hypotension in isoflurane anesthetized dogs. This study was approved by the Nihon University Animal Medical Center Research and Trial Ethics Committee (approval number: 1-007; approval date: September 29, 2022).

title: Management of shift work disorder: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine systematic review, meta-analysis, and GRADE assessment.
journal: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine
abstract: The purpose of this systematic review is to provide supporting evidence for a clinical practice guideline on the treatment of adults with shift work disorder (SWD). The American Academy of Sleep Medicine commissioned a task force of six experts in sleep and circadian medicine. A systematic review was conducted to identify randomized controlled trials, observational studies, and treatment trials in which treatments for the symptoms of excessive sleepiness and/or sleep disturbance/insomnia in adults with SWD, and for circadian adaptation to shift work schedules was tested. Evidence from controlled laboratory trials of simulated shift work and of field-based trials of shift workers with and without a diagnosis of SWD was included. Statistical analyses were performed to determine the significance of critical and important outcomes and clinically meaningful thresholds were set to determine the clinical relevance of treatments on the outcomes examined, where possible. Finally, the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) process was used to assess the evidence for making recommendations. The literature search resulted in 3,045 articles; 118 studies provided data suitable for statistical analyses. The task force provided a detailed summary of the evidence along with the quality of evidence, the balance of benefits and harms, patient values and preferences, and resource use considerations.

title: Contemporary bulk-fill restorative materials under simulated asthma inhalation therapy: a comparative assessment of surface stability.
abstract: To compare the surface stability of four contemporary bulk-fill restorative materials following simulated 21-day antiasthmatic inhalation therapy, and to investigate the relationships among the resulting surface changes. One hundred ninety-two disc-shaped specimens (8 × 2 mm) were prepared from four bulk-fill restorative materials: a nanofilled composite (Filtek One Bulk), an alkasite (Cention Forte), a giomer (Beautifil-Bulk) and a self-cure composite (Stela Capsule) (n = 8 per subgroup). Specimens were exposed once daily for 21 days via nebulizer to budesonide, fluticasone, salbutamol, budesonide + salbutamol, or fluticasone + salbutamol, while the control specimens were stored in artificial saliva. Changes in color (ΔE00), gloss, microhardness and surface roughness were assessed relative to baseline. Data were analyzed using two-way ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis tests and Spearman correlations (α = 0.05). Restorative material and inhaler group significantly affected all four parameters (p < 0.05). Salbutamol caused significantly greater changes than budesonide, fluticasone and the control in every material; the combination regimens were intermediate, and budesonide and fluticasone generally did not differ. The self-cure composite was the least stable and the nanofilled composite the most stable (except for color); microhardness loss increased significantly in the order Filtek One Bulk < Beautifil-Bulk < Cention Forte < Stela Capsule. All four surface parameters were strongly and positively correlated (ρ = 0.79-0.94; p < 0.001). Simulated antiasthmatic inhaler exposure degraded the surface of all bulk-fill materials in a material-dependent manner, with salbutamol exerting the greatest effect. The nanofilled composite showed the highest resistance. For asthmatic patients, and especially frequent salbutamol users, a highly filled light-cured nanofilled composite appears preferable to a self-cure bulk-fill composite where surface durability is clinically important.

title: Unlocking therapeutic potential of Wnt signaling pathway in neurodegenerative diseases.
abstract: The Wnt Signaling pathway is a regulatory network that is highly conserved in the central nervous system and is essential for the survival of neurons, synaptic plasticity, and the blood-brain barrier's integrity. The pathophysiology of major neurodegenerative and neurological disorders, including Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), Huntington's disease (HD), amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), and traumatic brain injury (TBI), is highly influenced by canonical and non-canonical Wnt Signaling dysregulation, according to increasingly compelling evidence. In addition to emphasising common molecular events such as GSK-3β overactivation, β-catenin destabilisation, neuroinflammation, synaptic dysfunction, and BBB disruption, this study offers a comparative and mechanistic overview of Wnt pathway changes across various illnesses. This article identifies overlapping treatment targets, such as GSK-3β, DKK1, LRP5/6, and Wnt ligands, by integrating common and disease-specific Wnt-associated pathways, in contrast to traditional disease-specific reviews. Furthermore, new translational approaches involving natural substances, Wnt modulators, and pathway-targeted treatments are critically examined. All things considered, this study presents Wnt Signaling as a potential neuroprotective and regenerative target for upcoming precision-based treatments in neurodegenerative disorders.

title: Development of cosmeceutical nanoemulsion formulation containing peptide acting on neurotransmitters and evaluation of its efficacy.
abstract: External factors such as oxidative stress and ultraviolet (UV) radiation increase reactive oxygen species (ROS) and cause the skin to age faster. Recently, peptides have been frequently preferred in nanoformulation development to prevent these effects. This study aimed to develop a nanoemulsion formulation of Syn-Ake peptide that reduces wrinkles by affecting neurotransmitters and to evaluate its efficacy by in silico and in vitro methods. In this context, the anti-aging activity of Syn-Ake peptide was evaluated by molecular docking and MD simulation. Then, nanoemulsion formulations of the peptide were produced using ultrasonic homogenization method and stability and characterization studies were conducted. The in vitro safety of the formulation was evaluated by genotoxicity and cytotoxicity studies. The cell regenerative effect of the formulation was evaluated by scratch test. Additionally, the protective effect of its formulation against H2O2-UV-induced skin damage was evaluated at both the cellular and DNA levels. Finally, the antioxidant activity and the collagenase inhibitory activity of the formulation was evaluated. Our findings showed that the peptide strongly interacted with p-38 MAPK and PI3K-AKT signalling pathways, as well as stromelysins and gelatinases. The most stable formulation was determined among the formulations developed with different production procedures. The formulation was determined to be non-genotoxic, cytocompatible and to have cell regenerative properties. It was also evaluated that the formulation was protective against H2O2-UV-based damage, showed antioxidant activity and collagenase inhibitory activity. The formulation of Syn-Ake peptide in nanoemulsion was evaluated to have promising potential as an anti-aging product candidate with a high efficacy and safety profile. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13205-026-05090-6.

title: A Blood-Based Synaptic Biomarker in Neuronally-Enriched Extracellular Vesicles Predicts Disability Progression in Progressive Multiple Sclerosis.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
abstract: Progressive multiple sclerosis (PMS) lacks blood-based biomarkers of the neurodegenerative processes driving disability. We measured synaptopodin, a postsynaptic protein, in neuronal-enriched extracellular vesicles (NEVs) across two independent cohorts: the SPRINT-MS trial (n=184) and a real-world validation cohort (n=268). A one SD increase in baseline synaptopodin was associated with ∼32% lower risk of confirmed disability progression in PMS (p=0.011), with the strongest effect in secondary PMS (SPMS) (∼57% lower odds, p=0.019). This SPMS association was replicated in the validation cohort (∼60% lower odds, p=0.009). Higher baseline synaptopodin was associated with future slower whole-brain atrophy and preserved microstructural integrity across MRI metrics (p=0.007-0.013). Longitudinal changes in NEV synaptopodin were associated with disability worsening (p=0.007) and paralleled MRI microstructural changes. NEV synaptopodin, but not NfL, was associated with confirmed disability progression in PMS participants with both biomarkers measured (HR 0.71 vs 1.12, p=0.007 vs 0.22 for NEV synaptopodin and NfL, respectively) and SPMS (HR 0.58 vs 1.10, p=0.003 vs 0.50). Adding synaptopodin, but not NfL, to a base model improved discrimination for disability progression in SPMS in both cohorts (e.g. validation AUC 0.755 to 0.838, p=0.005). These findings identify NEV synaptopodin as a prognostic and longitudinal, blood biomarker of synaptic integrity in PMS, particularly SPMS, complementing NfL.

title: Prenatal maternal inflammation and cognitive performance in offspring during late midlife.
abstract: Higher levels of prenatal maternal inflammation (PNMI) have been associated with offspring psychiatric disorders characterized by cognitive changes, and alterations in cognitive ability during early stages of development. Investigations into the effects of PNMI exposure and timing on cognitive outcomes in offspring later in life are lacking. Thus, the current study aimed to assess whether PNMI exposure in the first two trimesters was associated with offspring cognitive performance in late midlife. Participants were 137 mother-offspring dyads from the Child Health and Developmental Studies (CHDS) cohort that had maternal first and second trimester (T1, T2) sera data for interleukin- (IL-) 6, IL-8, IL-1 receptor antagonist (RA), and soluble tumor necrosis factor receptor-II (sTNF-RII), and an offspring follow-up assessment during late midlife (ages 57-62). Offspring underwent a battery of cognitive tests assessing verbal memory, general cognitive ability, verbal IQ, executive control, attention, working memory, and fine motor functioning. After controlling for maternal education to account for postnatal cognitive advantage, we identified a significant association between higher T1 PNMI and better performance on tasks of executive control (IL-8, Trails B-A, p = .003) and working memory (sTNF-RII, Digit-Span [DS] Backwards, p = .014). We also found significant associations between higher T2 PNMI and poorer performance on executive control (IL-6, Trails B-A, p = .002), working memory (IL-6, DS Backwards, p = .018), verbal IQ (IL-6, Wechsler Test of Adult Reading [WTAR], p = .039), and verbal memory (IL-8, Long Delay-Free Recall [LD-FR], p = .001). Such timing-specific associations of PNMI suggest that early gestational inflammatory exposure may be protective for some cognitive capacities, whereas mid-gestational exposure, especially to IL-6, suggests risk for decreases in memory and several other cognitive domains measurable in offspring approximately six decades later.

title: Decoding Alignment without Encoding Alignment: A critique of similarity analysis in neuroscience.
abstract: RSA and CKA are standard metrics for comparing neural representations across brain regions, organisms, and deep learning models. We demonstrate a fundamental weakness: these decoding-based metrics are insensitive to encoding manifold topology---the internal functional organization of a neural population. In a controlled MNIST experiment, RSA, CKA, and Procrustes $R^2$ remain statistically unchanged when encoding topology is causally manipulated via an auxiliary clustering loss, while the two model populations differ significantly in attribution patterns, weight-graph assortativity, and out-of-distribution robustness. Across biological systems and machine learning models, similar decoding behavior can arise from small, non-representative subpopulations, and alignment metrics are insensitive to encoding manifold topology even when it is fundamentally altered. These findings bear directly on mechanistic interpretability: standard alignment metrics cannot distinguish whether two networks share the same computational circuits or merely produce indistinguishable aggregate outputs. We propose encoding manifolds and Gromov-Wasserstein distance as complementary diagnostics for any decoding-based similarity claim, and provide a Neural Manifold Explorer tool at https://johannesbertram.github.io/FNN_Manifolds/index.html for further experimentation.

title: Mean Field Theory Based on the Spike Time Response Curve for Synchronization Within and Between Two Alternating Populations of Neural Oscillators with Delays.
abstract: In order to study oscillators coupled by pulses emitted at discrete times, it is generally assumed that the effect of each pulse is an instantaneous phase shift, with a possible conduction delay between emission and receipt. However, we are interested in neural oscillators in which each pulse (action potential) activates a biexponential synapse, and at high frequencies, the duration of the synaptic conductance may be greater than the network period. Therefore, the effect of received pulses can summate over the course of several cycles. To overcome this limitation, we previously defined a mean field approach for a single synchronous population. Here, we extend it to two alternating synchronous populations by assuming a perturbation of a single oscillator from one of the synchronous populations which is represented by a single self-connected neural oscillator. The train of delayed biexponential synapses emitted by each oscillator is divided into a tonic and a phasic component. Because of the continuous rather than pulsatile nature of the input, we had to drop the concept of oscillator phase and derive self-consistent criteria for the existence and stability of an alternating firing pattern between two synchronous populations based solely on the perturbation of time intervals from their steady state values. Simulations showed that for high frequency oscillations as defined above, the mean field approach predicts the existence and stability of phase-locking between two synchronous populations better than the instantaneous phase shift approach. This approach may generalize to other forms of coupling amongst non-neural oscillators.

title: Profiling Transcriptomic Changes Across Frontal Cortical Subregions in Major Depressive Disorder.
abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) involves frontal cortical dysfunction, with emerging evidence implicating gliovascular and immune mechanisms, yet its transcriptional signatures across subregions, cell-types, and molecular layers remain poorly defined. Here, we integrated bulk-tissue RNA-seq data from dlPFC, mPFC, and dACC (n = 286) to identify a conserved core transcriptional profile, anchored in downregulated interneuron markers, and upregulated immune and vascular genes, spatially enriched in leptomeninges and white matter. Concordantly, multiomic factor analysis revealed immune activation, stress-response, and accelerated aging in MDD. Analysis of snRNA-seq data from dlPFC, mPFC, and oFC (863,511 nuclei; n = 204) revealed most pronounced MDD signatures in excitatory neurons, accompanied by coordinated disruption of glucocorticoid receptor machinery across cell-types, including FKBP5 upregulation. Glial, immune, and perivascular populations exhibited signatures of oxidative stress, ECM remodeling, and reduced neuronal support, and greater concordance with bulk-tissue MDD signals than neurons. A global reduction in cell-to-cell communications in MDD revealed a shift from homeostatic neuronal signaling toward endothelial and myelination-associated pathways. Ephrin-Eph signaling was consistently dysregulated, implicating disrupted axonal guidance, synaptic remodeling, and neurovascular integrity. Notably, MDD signatures were shared between MDD-only and PTSD comorbid cases at bulk-tissue analyses, while diverging at single-cell resolution. Together, these findings reframe MDD as a distributed frontal cortex disorder, driven by disrupted neuroglial and neurovascular communication.

title: Outcomes of patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis admitted to the ICU for acute respiratory failure.
abstract: Data on patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) for acute respiratory failure are scarce, and early prognostic markers are lacking. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients with ALS admitted for acute respiratory failure to two ICUs of a tertiary referral center between 2016 and 2022. The primary outcome was 3-month mortality. Factors associated with 3-month mortality were assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. Survival and functional outcomes were evaluated up to 12 months. Among 139 patients [median age 66 (IQR 57-73) years, 61.2% being men], 109 (78.4%) patients presented with hypercapnia and 82 (59.0%) with hypoxemia (defined as PaO₂/FiO₂ ratio < 300) at ICU admission, with frequent overlap between both conditions. Non-invasive ventilation was used in 79.9% of patients, while 13.7% were intubated, and 2.2% underwent tracheostomy. Three-month mortality was 48.2%, increasing to 61.2% and 74.1% at 6 and 12 months respectively. In multivariable analysis, hypoxemia at ICU admission was independently associated with increased 3-month mortality (HR = 2.27, 95% CI: 1.28-4.01; P = 0.005), along with older age (HR=1.03 per year, 95% CI: 1.00-1.06; P = 0.035). Among patients alive at 3 months, a majority (79.2%) were living at home. ICU admission for acute respiratory failure in ALS is associated with substantial short-term mortality, consistent with the poor prognosis inherent to the natural history of the disease. Hypoxemia at admission identifies a subgroup at particularly high risk of death and may help inform early prognostic assessment and shared decision-making. However, patients who survive the acute ICU phase frequently achieve favorable short-term outcomes, with most living at home at 3 months.

title: Brain-Targeted Epigenome-Wide Association Study of Childhood Internalizing and Externalizing Behaviors: Evidence from a Monozygotic Twin Cohort.
abstract: Background Identifying biologically meaningful epigenetic signatures of childhood internalizing and externalizing behaviors has been challenging because conventional epigenome-wide association studies are limited by small effect sizes, genetic confounding, and uncertain tissue relevance. We therefore combined a brain-targeted epigenome-wide association study (BEWAS) with a monozygotic twin difference design to improve biological specificity while isolating environmentally driven DNA methylation patterns. Methods Buccal-derived DNA methylation was analyzed in 415 children from the Arizona Twin Project, including 102 monozygotic twin pairs. DNA methylation analyses were restricted to genes with elevated brain expression or established roles in neurotransmission. Linear mixed-effects models were conducted in the full sample, followed by within-pair MZ difference analyses. Nominally associated CpG sites underwent pathway enrichment analyses, and gene-level findings were compared with previous pediatric DNA methylation studies. Results Although no individual CpG sites survived epigenome-wide correction, nominally associated loci converged on robust neurodevelopmental pathways involved in neurogenesis, neuronal differentiation, synaptic organization, and neuronal projection development. Internalizing behaviors demonstrated pathway enrichment in both the population-based and MZ analyses, whereas externalizing enrichment emerged only in the MZ analyses despite the substantially smaller sample size. Gene-level overlap with previous pediatric methylation studies was greater in the MZ analyses, with recurrent associations observed for neurodevelopmental genes including PTPRN2 , SHANK2 , CACNA1C , and ADCY8 . Overall, convergence emerged primarily at the level of genes and biological pathways rather than individual CpG sites. Conclusions These findings suggest that childhood internalizing and externalizing behaviors are characterized by distributed epigenetic regulation across neurodevelopmental systems. More broadly, they demonstrate how biologically informed epigenomic restriction combined with genetically informative study designs can improve detection and interpretation of molecular signatures relevant to developmental psychopathology, providing a foundation for future biomarker discovery and precision mental health approaches.

title: TLR7-mediated autoimmunity targets Robo3 to drive astrogliosis in frontotemporal dementia.
abstract: Mutations in GRN and C9orf72 are common causes of frontotemporal dementia (FTD). While it is well-recognized that GRN or C9orf72 mutations also increase the risk of autoimmune diseases, the intersection of innate and adaptive immunity, neuroinflammation, and neurodegeneration in FTD remains unclear. Here we show that concurrent loss of Grn and C9orf72 breaks immune tolerance by activating the pattern recognition receptor, TLR7, leading to clonal expansion of age-associated B cells and activated B cells. Grn-/-;C9orf72-/- B cells exhibited heightened responses upon TLR7 activation and produced autoantibodies that target the axon guidance receptor Robo3 to promote astroglial pathology. Interestingly, immunization with Robo3 extracellular domain in young Grn-/-;C9orf72-/- mice accelerated astrogliosis. Conversely, TLR7 antagonist M5049 treatment rescued B cell defects, reduced anti-Robo3 autoantibodies, and mitigated astrogliosis and synaptic loss in Grn-/-;C9orf72-/- mice. Together, these results offer critical insights into how TLR7-mediated autoimmune dysfunction targets Robo3 to drive neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration in FTD.

title: Trigeminal nerve microstructure in chronic temporomandibular joint pain: A diffusion tensor imaging study.
journal: Journal of oral biology and craniofacial research
abstract: To evaluate whether chronic temporomandibular joint (TMJ) pain secondary to internal joint disorders is associated with microstructural alterations of the trigeminal nerve (TN), assessed by diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and fractional anisotropy (FA). Forty individuals were included: 20 patients with chronic TMJ pain and 20 pain-free controls. All participants underwent magnetic resonance imaging with DTI focused on the cisternal segment of the TN. FA values were measured bilaterally. Between-group comparisons were performed using Mann-Whitney tests, and associations between FA and clinical variables were assessed using Spearman rank correlations. No significant side-to-side FA difference was observed in controls (P = 0.20), and no significant FA difference was detected between painful TMJs and control sides (P = 0.75). FA was not associated with pain duration (P = 0.50) or pain intensity during mandibular function (P = 0.64). In contrast, among TMJs with pain at rest, greater resting pain intensity was significantly associated with lower ipsilateral TN FA (21 TMJs from 15 patients; Spearman ρ = -0.51, P = 0.019). Chronic TMJ pain secondary to internal joint disorders was not associated with a detectable global reduction in cisternal TN FA. However, the inverse association between resting pain intensity and ipsilateral FA suggests subtle pain-related microstructural variation in a clinically relevant subgroup. These findings support further investigation of trigeminal neuroplasticity in persistent TMJ pain while avoiding interpretation of FA as a direct marker of structural nerve damage.

title: Cell-type-resolved mRNA 3'-end remodeling in Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Alternative polyadenylation diversifies messenger RNAs by altering coding sequences and 3' untranslated regions, but its organization across human brain cell types and disruption in neurodegeneration remain poorly understood. By analyzing 3'-capture single-nucleus RNA sequencing data of 6.3 million nuclei from the prefrontal cortex of 1,494 human donors, we defined 108,768 polyadenylation sites across 25,274 genes, most of which were absent from the GENCODE polyadenylation-site annotation. Polyadenylation-site usage was strongly cell-type-specific and revealed regulatory differences not captured by gene expression. With increasing Alzheimer's disease clinicopathological severity, excitatory neurons, oligodendrocytes and immune cells showed increased distal-site preference, including reduced relative usage of intronic sites and increased distal 3' untranslated region usage in synaptic and RNA-processing genes. External single-nucleus data supported neuronal and oligodendrocyte patterns, while complementary analyses of purified microglia supported selected immune-cell findings. Integrative analyses of cleavage and polyadenylation factor expression, co-regulated usage networks, sequence motifs and published perturbations prioritized the cleavage factor Im complex as a candidate regulator. These findings identify cell-type-specific messenger RNA 3'-end remodeling as a reproducible dimension of Alzheimer's disease molecular pathology that is only partly captured by gene-level analyses.

title: Brain region- and solubility-dependent proteomic signatures of neurofibrillary tangle pathology in Alzheimer's disease.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
abstract: Neurofibrillary tangles (NFTs) containing hyperphosphorylated tau proteins are a hallmark neuropathology of Alzheimer's disease. However, the molecular basis underlying their spatial heterogeneity and biochemical complexity remain unclear. To address this, we performed mass spectrometry-based proteomic profiling of two neocortical regions with different susceptibilities to NFT pathology-the inferior temporal (IT) and middle frontal (MF) cortices-from 27 autopsy cases stratified by Braak NFT stage (Low 0-II, n=8; Mid III-IV, n=11; High V-VI, n=8). Brain homogenates were sequentially fractionated using buffers of increasing solubility (TBS, Na₂CO₃, and Urea), followed by trypsin digestion and analysis by nanoLC-MS/MS with data-independent acquisition. Proteins were identified using PEAKS Studio 12 and linear mixed-effects models were applied to assess Braak stage-associated and region-specific changes in protein abundance and solubility. A total of 5,573 protein groups were identified, including 452 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs), 183 bidirectional expression proteins (BEPs), and 693 differentially soluble proteins (DSPs) associated with NFT pathology. These proteins were enriched in pathways related to cytoskeletal organization, synaptic transmission, metabolism, vesicular trafficking, and proteostasis. Marked regional differences were observed, with limited overlap between IT and MF across DEPs, BEPs, and DSPs. Protein change in MF was dynamic with a higher number of BEPs and suggested active cytoskeletal remodeling, whereas IT showed fewer BEPs and evidence of structural disruption, including alterations in intermediate filament components, consistent with vulnerability of IT and possible compensatory/plasticity changes in MF cortex. MF cortex had the greatest downregulation of DEPs between Low and Mid Braak stages, while the transition from Mid to High Braak stage showed upregulation of most of DEPs in both regions. In addition, widespread changes in protein solubility were observed, particularly decreased solubility at later Braak stages, implicating disruption of proteostasis. Together, these findings highlight region- and stage-dependent proteomic alterations associated with tau pathology and underscore their relevance for understanding disease mechanisms and informing biomarker development.

title: Neuroplasticity-Based Treatment Prioritization in Major Depressive Disorder: A Two-Cohort Study.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
abstract: Antidepressant selection in major depressive disorder remains trial-and-error, and no biomarker identifies which drug will work for an individual patient. Because neuroplasticity is a convergent mechanism of antidepressant response, we tested whether it could serve as a drug-specific biomarker in patient-derived neurons. We developed the Neuroplasticity Score (NPS), integrating structural and synaptic features from high-content imaging of patient-derived cortical neurons, and validated it against graded brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) exposure in neurons from 16 healthy donors. NPS was then applied unmodified to 75 antidepressant treatment episodes from 44 patients across two independent retrospective cohorts: 40 episodes from 20 STAR*D participants (Cohort 1; USA multi-site) and 35 episodes from 24 participants at Sheba Medical Center and Geha Mental Health Center (Cohort 2; Israel). NPS increased with escalating BDNF dose (Spearman ρ=0.83; P<.001). Response rate rose monotonically across NPS tertiles in both cohorts (trend P=.001 and P<.001). Across all 75 episodes, 84.6% of episodes in the highest NPS tertile responded, compared to 48.0% overall. NPS discriminated responding from non-responding episodes with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.81 in both cohorts. The pooled odds ratio per 1-SD increase was 6.05 (95% CI, 2.80-13.05; I²=26%). Within patients contributing both a responding and a non-responding episode, the highest-scoring drug was the one that worked in 86% of patients (P<.001). Higher antidepressant-induced neuroplasticity in a patient's own neurons corresponded to a higher likelihood of response to that specific drug across two independent cohorts.

title: Treatment restrictions after acute stroke across nine European countries and their association with 90-day mortality: a post hoc analysis of the PRECIOUS randomised controlled trial.
abstract: In patients with acute stroke, early withholding or withdrawal of life-sustaining therapies is associated with an increased risk of death. We used practice variation across nine European countries to assess whether this relation may be causal. We performed a post hoc analysis of the PREvention of Complications to Improve OUtcome in elderly patients with acute Stroke (PRECIOUS) trial, a randomised clinical trial of metoclopramide, paracetamol, and/or ceftriaxone started within 24 h of symptom onset in older patients with acute ischaemic stroke or intracerebral haemorrhage (ISRCTN82217627). The frequency of early treatment restrictions, defined as those installed within 24 h after randomisation, was calculated per participating country and their relation with the primary outcome 'death at 90 days' was estimated through: 1) adjustment for confounders with regression analysis with inverse-propensity score reweighting; and 2) comparing patients enrolled in countries with and without early restrictions, adjusted for confounders with regression analysis. Of 1493 patients enrolled in PRECIOUS between 2016 and 2022, 1451/1493 (97%) were included in this analysis, of whom 276/1451 (19%) had an early treatment restriction. The rate of these restrictions ranged from 0% to 48% across the participating countries. Patients with restrictions were more likely to die within 90 days (inverse propensity-weighted odds ratio (OR) 3.39; 95% CI 2.71-4.25). However, there was no difference in the rate of death at 90 days between countries with and those without restrictions (21.3% vs 23.5%, adjusted OR 1.39; 95% CI 0.8-2.39). The use of treatment restrictions early after stroke varied widely across Europe. Although restrictions were independently associated with an increased rate of death, the comparison of death rates between countries with and those without such restrictions provides no indication that this relation is causal. European Union's Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme; grant agreement No. 634809.

title: Astrocytic timekeepers and their influence on brain waste clearance in Alzheimer's disease.
journal: Neurobiology of sleep and circadian rhythms
abstract: Alzheimer's disease is associated with disruptions in circadian rhythmicity, yet the underlying mechanisms remain only partially understood. Developing insights suggest that astrocytes possess their own intrinsic circadian clocks, influencing multiple functions in brain homeostasis. Given the central role of astrocytes in brain waste clearance, this review investigates how the astrocytic clock mediates brain waste clearance and contributes to Alzheimer's disease pathology. By reviewing recent findings on extracellular clearance, cellular protein homeostasis, cellular detoxification/redox defence and neurotransmitter homeostasis, this review bridges research on astrocytic clock disruption with altered brain waste clearance dynamics. It further highlights the relevance of these alterations to Alzheimer's disease pathology. Interestingly, some clock-gene disruptions are associated with markers suggestive of increased autophagic activity and glymphatic-related gene expression, which may represent a compensatory response to circadian clock alteration. However, whether these changes translate into improved functional clearance in vivo, and whether they meaningfully affect Alzheimer's disease progression, remains uncertain. In contrast, similar clock-gene alterations generally impair blood-brain barrier integrity, glutamate clearance and antioxidant response, decreasing waste clearance capacity. These findings suggest a possible bidirectional relationship, in which some pathways may partially compensate for impairments in others. However, it remains unclear to what extent an imbalance in these pathways contributes to the development and/or progression of Alzheimer's disease. Altogether, the astrocytic circadian clock is positioned as an important regulator of brain waste clearance and warrants future mechanistic and therapeutic investigation.

title: Ancient somatosensory circuit architectures employ flexible molecular strategies.
abstract: The extent to which conserved neural circuit architectures depend on shared molecular specification programs remains unclear. Here, we address this question by examining the somatosensory system of the little skate, Leucoraja erinacea, an early-diverging vertebrate that retains ancestral features of both finned and limb-based body plans. We show that core features of somatosensory circuit organization, including laminar organization of the spinal cord and dorsally restricted targeting of sensory afferents, are deeply conserved. Unexpectedly, the molecular programs specifying dorsal root ganglion (DRG) sensory subtypes diverge extensively from those of mammals. Although DRG neuron subtype specification and spinal connectivity rely on target-derived cues, skates employ distinct neurotrophin receptor and transcription factor identity codes. These findings support a model in which conserved spinal circuit architectures provide a stable scaffold that leverages flexible sensory neuron specification programs, enabling the evolutionary diversification of vertebrate somatosensory systems.

title: Analytical performance of a delayed-centrifugation blood collection tube for remote blood biomarker assessment.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
abstract: Current biobanking guidelines require in-person blood collection and immediate processing for Alzheimer's disease (AD) biomarker assessment. We recently reported that the P100 blood collection tubes containing protease inhibitors improve protein biomarker stability over delayed centrifugation periods. However, whether this comparability extends beyond a small set of biomarkers to the broad panels enabled by high-plex platforms has not been established. Here, we performed a head-to-head comparison of 127 neurodegeneration-related biomarkers in paired P100 vs. standard ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) plasma samples from n = 43 community-dwelling older adult participants using the NUcleic acid-Linked Immuno-Sandwich Assay (NULISA) proteomic technology. The NULISA assay demonstrated excellent technical reproducibility (intra- and inter-plate coefficients of variation [CVs] 0.8) with minimal mean differences and no significant proportional bias in Bland-Altman analysis, including plasma Aβ42, GFAP, MAPT, NEFL, p-tau181, and p-tau231, while p-tau217 showed a P100-EDTA correlation of ρ = 0.57. Two biomarker ratios (Aβ42/Aβ40 and p-tau217/Aβ42) also showed minimal bias with no proportional bias detected. Receiver operating characteristic analysis using amyloid status, assessed with positron emission tomography in a subset of participants, showed comparable classification performance between the two tube types, with classification concordance up to 92% and no significant DeLong differences for most (80%) biomarkers. These findings indicate that, on the NULISA platform, P100 tubes yield analytical and classification performance comparable to conventional EDTA tubes, supporting their use for blood-based neurodegeneration biomarker research where immediate sample processing is not feasible.

title: Cell type specific enrichment of substance use and substance use disorder heritability.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
abstract: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified numerous loci associated with substance use disorders (SUDs). To connect common genetic variation to cell type- and region-specific gene expression and chromatin accessibility, we examined the enrichment of genetic liability for several SUDs (alcohol, cannabis, tobacco, and opioid use disorders) and substance consumption phenotypes (drinks per week, cannabis ever-use, and cigarettes per day) in available single-nucleus RNAseq data spanning 10 brain regions and snATACseq data spanning 42 brain regions. Significant cell-type enrichment after multiple testing corrections was observed only for drinks per week and tobacco use disorder in the snRNAseq data and for cannabis use disorder and problematic alcohol use in snATACseq data. Across both transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility annotations, enrichment patterns were concentrated in excitatory neuronal populations, particularly upper layer intratelencephalic neurons, amygdala excitatory neurons, and regionally resolved striatal medium spiny neuron subtypes. Drinks per week, problematic alcohol use, and cannabis use disorder showed enrichment values that were significantly correlated within cell-type across snRNAseq and snATACseq, suggesting convergent biological signals across independent single-nucleus modalities. These findings implicate chromatin-mediated expression differences in specific excitatory neuronal populations as potential mediators of SUD genetic liability and highlight the value of integrating transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility data for characterising the neurobiology of addiction.

title: Cross-Tissue Inflammatory Convergence Supports a Putative Muscle-Brain Axis in Alzheimer's Disease.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
abstract: Reduced muscle strength is associated with cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease (AD), suggesting that skeletal-muscle aging and AD-related neurodegeneration may share biological mechanisms. Vascular dysfunction, immune activation, and extracellular-matrix remodeling have been implicated in both tissues, but the extent of shared cellular and molecular programs remains unclear. We investigated cross-tissue transcriptional programs in aging skeletal muscle and AD-related brain tissue and evaluated whether related signals are detectable in peripheral blood. We analyzed independent, unpaired human transcriptomic datasets from skeletal muscle (23 donors), the SEA-AD middle temporal gyrus atlas (84 donors), and peripheral blood. Donor-aware models identified age-associated changes in muscle and transcriptomic changes across continuous pseudoprogression score (CPS) in brain. Cross-tissue comparisons focused on 30 brain donors within an early CPS window. Shared tissue-derived programs were assessed in peripheral blood mononuclear cells and independently tested in frailty bulk-blood and Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) whole-blood datasets. CellOracle simulations were used to prioritize candidate transcriptional regulators. Aging muscle showed increased inflammatory, extracellular-matrix, and stromal communication programs. During early AD-related brain progression, vascular and immune populations showed increasing inflammatory and matrix-associated activity together with shifts in intercellular communication. Cross-tissue analysis identified six concordantly enriched pathways comprising 109 leading-edge genes in endothelial populations and four pathways comprising 51 genes in myeloid populations. Related peripheral-blood signatures varied across cohorts and cell types. However, in independent frailty and ADNI mild cognitive impairment and AD datasets, 23 of 30 predefined tissue-derived pathway-subset tests showed significant positive enrichment after false-discovery-rate correction, whereas individual gene-level bulk-blood associations did not survive correction. CellOracle analyses prioritized ETS2 and BHLHE40 as exploratory endothelial regulators whose simulated perturbation consistently reduced selected shared program scores across tissues. Aging skeletal muscle and AD-related brain tissue exhibit convergent endothelial and myeloid inflammatory programs, with related pathway-level signals detectable in peripheral blood. These cross-tissue programs and candidate endothelial regulators provide testable hypotheses for mechanisms linking systemic aging, muscle dysfunction, and AD-related neurodegeneration.

title: A biomimetic gas-protein co-delivery nanoplatform targets mitochondrial stress and GSDME activation for glioblastoma immunotherapy.
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains one of the most aggressive primary brain malignancies, with the therapeutic efficacy of conventional treatments and cancer immunotherapy being severely hindered by the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and the highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Although pyroptosis, an inflammatory form of programmed cell death, can elicit potent antitumor immunity through the release of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs), the precise induction of pyroptosis and the amplification of its immunostimulatory effects remain major challenges. Herein, we developed a biomimetic microglial cell membrane-coated nanosystem (M@GM) that integrates brain-targeted delivery, mitochondria-mediated damage, and innate immune activation for cascade-enhanced glioblastoma therapy. The nanosystem consists of a manganese carbonyl (MnCO) core loaded with Gasdermin E (GSDME) and cloaked with a microglial cell membrane, enabling efficient BBB penetration and active GBM targeting. Upon accumulation within the tumor microenvironment, M@GM responsively releases CO, Mn2+, and GSDME. CO and Mn2+ induced mitochondrial stress and ROS accumulation, which were accompanied by activation of the Caspase-3/GSDME axis and pyroptosis-associated cell death. The associated HMGB1 release and CRT exposure are consistent with an immunogenic cell death (ICD)-related response, while Mn2+ cooperatively activates the cGAS-STING innate immune pathway, promoting dendritic cell maturation, effector T-cell infiltration, and M1 polarization of tumor-associated macrophages, ultimately converting the immunologically "cold" GBM microenvironment into an immune-active "hot" phenotype. Both in vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated enhanced BBB transport and brain accumulation of M@GM, significantly inhibited GBM progression, prolonged the survival of tumor-bearing mice, and exhibited favorable biosafety. This work presents a biomimetic therapeutic strategy based on "biomimetic delivery-pyroptosis amplification-immune remodeling", providing a promising design paradigm for brain-targeted nanomedicine-enabled cancer immunotherapy.

title: A CNS-targeted atovaquone nanotherapy mitigates complement activation and neuromuscular degeneration in ALS.
abstract: Complement-mediated glial inflammation and synaptic injury are increasingly implicated in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), but clinically translatable complement-modulating therapies remain limited. Atovaquone (ATQ) is an approved, poorly water-soluble small molecule with reported immunomodulatory activity. We investigated whether ATQ could modulate C1qb or C5aR1-associated pathology and whether lactoferrin (Lf)-derived nanomicelles could improve delivery to the spinal cord. ALS spinal-cord single-cell transcriptomic and pathway-enrichment analyses were combined with screening of an FDA-approved drug library, molecular docking and surface plasmon resonance (SPR). Lf-ATQ nanomicelles were characterised by dynamic light scattering, transmission electron microscopy and fluorescence distribution studies. Complement/inflammasome responses were examined in microglial and motor-neuron-microglia models. Therapeutic effects were evaluated in mice expressing the human superoxide dismutase 1 G93A variant (SOD1G93A) by motor testing, compound muscle action potential recording, histology, immunostaining, western blotting and proteomics. Complement genes, particularly C1qb and C5aR1, were enriched in microglia, whereas glutamatergic-synapse and axon-guidance programmes were negatively enriched. In cellular models and SOD1G93A spinal cord, Lf-ATQ reduced C1qb, NLRP3 and multiple inflammatory mediators, attenuated glial reactivity and altered autophagy-related proteins. Treatment preserved rotarod performance, grip strength, gait parameters, compound muscle action potential amplitude and gastrocnemius morphology. Proteomic analysis indicated remodelling of complement/coagulation, vesicular-transport and synaptic modules. These findings support Lf-ATQ as a central nervous system (CNS) -oriented, complement-regulating nanotherapy candidate for ALS. Direct functional target-inhibition assays, quantitative ATQ pharmacokinetics, long-term safety assessment and validation in non-SOD1 models remain necessary before translational conclusions can be drawn.

title: A Hypothalamic Pathway for Energy Conservation.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
abstract: Many animals utilize a survival strategy of hypothermia, inactivity, and a dramatic decrease in their energy metabolism when faced with a shortfall in energy supplies. Mice, for example, show daily torpor that may last several hours to bridge the lack of energy availability in a cold environment. While our recent studies identified a population of neurons in the median preoptic nucleus (MnPO) necessary for fasting-induced torpor regulation, the specific brain circuits that trigger energy conservation in response to food restriction are unknown. We show here that the energy state of the animal is conveyed to preoptic neurons by inputs from the arcuate nucleus (ARC), a region known to be indispensable for driving metabolic and behavioral adaptations to the fasted state. We first found that the activity of ARC neurons expressing Agouti-Related Peptide (ARC AgRP ) is required for the generation of fasting-induced torpor. Then, we showed that torpor-active ARC AgRP neurons innervate the preoptic area of the hypothalamus (POA), including the MnPO. Using optogenetic methods, we also found that activating the ARC AgRP →MnPO pathway induces key features of torpor: decreased body temperature, bradycardia, reduction of energy expenditure, and suppression of brown adipose tissue thermogenesis. Remarkably, we also show that inhibition of the ARC AgRP →MnPO brain circuit entirely prevents fasting-induced torpor. Furthermore, we identified that both NPY and GABA are neuromodulators used by ARC AgRP neurons to enable hypothermic responses during starvation. Our studies provide a detailed view of a hypothalamic pathway enabling energy conservation, a survival mechanism in conditions of low energy availability.

title: Conservation of gene co-expression networks and neuropsychiatric-neurological disease gene programs between mouse and human frontal cortex at single-cell resolution.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
abstract: Mouse models are widely used in translational neuroscience, but whether a gene has the same partners in mouse and human prefrontal cortex (PFC) is unknown. The genes whose expression rises and falls with a given gene across samples (its co-expression partners) indicate the molecular program to which it belongs. We compared the co-expression of 13,214 genes between mouse medial PFC and human dorsolateral PFC in 246,211 single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-sequencing profiles. These two regions are not homologous, so part of any measured difference may reflect region and not species. The partners of single genes were only modestly similar in the two species, whereas groups of co-expressed genes (modules) were strongly preserved, and the higher conservation of disease genes was largely accounted for by general gene properties. We report five findings. First, the median similarity of partners for single genes was 0.169 (0, unrelated; 1, identical). This median was below that of every comparison among human datasets but within the range of comparisons among mouse datasets, and correction for measurement noise raised it to 0.349 at most. Second, all four mouse modules and four of five human modules were strongly preserved in the other species. Third, neuropsychiatric disease genes were modestly more conserved than other genes, but no more than control genes matched for mutational constraint and expression. None of the 14 disease genes had fewer cross-species partners than connectivity-matched comparison genes. Fifth, in an independent human dataset, four of five human modules defined on the 5,000 most variable genes recurred. We also identified two sources of error: analyzing only the most variable genes excludes most disease genes, and networks built from few samples, as for glial cells, underestimate the similarity between species. Scores and code are released for cross-species studies.

title: Carbonic anhydrase inhibition rescues heart function in the Tg2576 Alzheimer's mouse model by ameliorating cardiac amyloid-β pathology and neurotrophic-signaling impairment.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
abstract: FDA-approved carbonic anhydrase inhibitors (CAIs) have shown robust efficacy in reducing amyloid-β (Aβ) pathology, neurodegeneration, and cerebrovascular dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) models, highlighting carbonic anhydrase (CAs) as a promising, previously untapped therapeutic target for AD and vascular contribution to dementia. We have recently shown that Aβ aggregates disrupt neuro-signaling and deplete neurotrophic factors (particularly BDNF) in the heart of AD mouse models and human subjects. In this study, we present the first in-depth examination of CAI therapy (acetazolamide-ATZ) in Tg2576 mice, a well-established model of AD and CAA. We confirm that progressive cardiac fibrosis and Aβ deposition in 13-month-old mice severely impair the cardiac neuro-signaling system, marked by a drastic decrease in BDNF and reductions in adrenergic fibers and regenerating nerve endings (TH and GAP-43 markers), leading to significant declines in ejection fraction and fractional shortening compared to age-matched WT littermates. Critically, this study demonstrates that long-term ATZ treatment in Tg2576 mice significantly reduces cardiac Aβ burden, prevents adverse neuro-signaling remodeling, and restores heart physiological function, as assessed via speckle tracking strain echocardiography. These in vivo findings were corroborated in human cardiomyocytes, in which CA inhibition reduced human Aβ40 oligomer-dependent disruption of CREB signaling, thus preserving BDNF expression. Together, these results reveal a previously unrecognized cardio-neuroprotective role for CAIs in preventing Aβ-induced cardiovascular remodeling and neuro-signaling disruption in the Tg2576-AD model. Given the established benefits of CAIs on cerebrovascular function and cognition, our findings further support advancing repurposing efforts into clinical trials. CAIs such as ATZ could offer a dual-action therapy approach, addressing both the central nervous system and cardiac pathologies associated with AD and, potentially, the systemic effects of amyloidosis.

title: MTHFR*677C>T produces distinct prodromal disease signatures in a mouse model of late-onset Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Background Late-onset Alzheimer's disease (LOAD) comprises more than 95% of all AD cases. Transgenic, overexpression animal models have off-target side effects, do not effectively produce the heterogeneity observed clinically in LOAD patients, and are therefore not best suited for preclinical therapeutic development. The Model Organism Development and Evaluation for Late-onset Alzheimer's Disease (MODEL-AD) Consortium was established to develop novel mouse strains to model human-relevant genetic and environmental risk factors for LOAD. Methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) is an enzyme in the folate/methionine pathway. Variants in the MTHFR gene, notably 677C > T , are associated with ADRD, and we have previously shown the Mthfr 677C>T mouse model phenocopies humans carrying the variant and develops cerebrovascular deficits. Methods To examine the contributions of Mthfr 677C>T in the context of late-onset Alzheimer's disease (LOAD), MODEL-AD created a novel mouse strain on the C57BL/6J (B6) background that was homozygous for Mthfr 677C>T , in combination with humanized Aβ , APOEe4 , and Trem2*R47H ( referred to as LOAD2.Mthfr 677C>T ) . Mice were assessed over multiple ages for disease-relevant phenotypes. Regular behavior measurements and biometric samples were collected longitudinally to 24 months of age. Blood and brain tissue were collected for transcriptomics, proteomics, human disease correlation, and neuropathology. Results Despite lacking hallmark pathologies such as amyloid deposition and significant neuroinflammation, compared to LOAD2 controls, LOAD2.Mthfr 677C>T mice showed transcriptional and proteomic signatures in the brain that relate to the cerebrovasculature, myelination, and synaptic biology, similar to those seen in human LOAD patients. Conclusions These data further support the use of the LOAD2.Mthfr 677C>T mouse model to study aspects of ADRD such as cerebrovascular compromise.

title: Hemispheric Complementarity is Associated with Distinct Functional and Structural Brain Profiles.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
abstract: Hemispheric specialization is thought to follow a principle of complementarity, with homotopic functions such as language and attention lateralizing to opposite hemispheres, yet its consistency across individuals and relevance for cognition remain unclear. Using multimodal neuroimaging and twin-family data from 987 Human Connectome Project participants, we identified three sustained attentional lateralization phenotypes (right, left, bilateral) that were independent of handedness, differed by sex, and tracked broad shifts in brain organization, with bilateral individuals showing stronger intrahemispheric and homotopic connectivity. Examining attention and language revealed three multidomain profiles (crowded, mixed, split) reflecting whether functions colocalize within or are distributed across hemispheres. Mixed organization was linked to higher planum polare myelination, whereas crowded organization showed higher fiber density connectivity across dorsal attention-default network. Both phenotypes were heritable, yet neither predicted cognitive performance. These findings reveal a brain organization in which specialization emerges from flexible, heritable patterns linking function, structural connectivity, and myeloarchitecture.
